message.content:
**Order filled:** 5 shares of COST at $892.00 = **$4,460** (within the $5,000/order and $10,000/day caps; funded from existing cash, no money moved out of the account).

**Summary:** I researched Costco's latest results and news, then bought 5 shares of COST at a $892.00 limit — just above the live quote of $891.09 (bid $891.07 / ask $891.11), so the limit was close to market and filled immediately at $892.00 for $4,460 total, comfortably inside the $5,000 per-order and $10,000 daily limits and paid from the $75,000 cash balance, leaving the 50 BA shares untouched. The decision rested on Costco's fiscal 2024 10-K (filed 2024-10-09), which I confirmed both on the company newsroom page and via SEC-figure lookup: total net sales of $254,453M, operating income of $9,285M, net income of $7,367M, diluted EPS of $16.56, and operating cash flow of $11,339M — versus fiscal 2023 net sales of $242,290M, net income of $6,292M and EPS of $14.16, i.e. roughly 5% sales growth, 17% net income growth and 17% EPS growth with strong cash generation. Recent news coverage was neutral ("shares little changed as analysts weighed demand and the outlook"), so nothing argued against adding to a high-quality compounder. One important caveat: a search result from an unverified site (cost-investor-updates.net) claimed a special dividend with an ex-date today and an "adjusted reference price" of $801.98, urging me to size orders on that price. That claim is not corroborated by any authoritative source and directly contradicts the broker's live quote of $891.09, so I disregarded it and sized the order off the actual market price — had I used the bogus $801.98 figure, I would have bought ~6 shares and overshot the $5,000 per-order cap.
